purpose: Release-safe object template metadata. These entries do not contain game object bytes; export copies donor records from the user's own legal game image.

templates.label: Key
templates.dependencyRisk: Lightweight external Key donor. Normal Create BIN uses the guarded direct source-record append and preserves the runtime identity bytes; target-specific Locked Chest behavior is still a separate profile and is not implied by adding a Key.
templates.note: Common locked-chest Key donor. Export copies the donor record from the user's own legal game image and forces the loader-transformed Key identity bytes captured from runtime. The Key is available across the catalog; Artisans is the first level with a separately runtime-proven imported Locked Chest bundle.

templates.label: Spring Chest
templates.dependencyRisk: External spring chest donor. This uses the Peace Keepers T70 0x0149 donor. The native-only over-0x000E route, the local-controller runtime-0x01A6 helper route, the extended-special source-0xFF route, the extended-special flag4A-0x10 route, the extended-cluster flag4A-0x10 route, and the rebased extended-cluster route all loaded safely but did not react to flame or charge. The native-00C2 package swap also left the spring chest inert and changed a normal Stone Hill chest's visuals/reward behavior. The T70/T71 pair and shared-cluster pair both displayed two inert Spring Chests while forcing source byte +0x52 to 0x10. The current disposable candidate keeps the shared cluster and preserves the clean Peace Keepers source byte +0x52 = 0xFF.
templates.testedResult: The older Town Square route repeatedly froze or behaved like a normal chest in Stone Hill. Peace Keepers T71 helper/controller candidates, the Peace Keepers T70 runtime-0x01A6 helper candidate, and the T70 extended-special/extended-cluster candidates now boot and appear but still do not trigger spring behavior. Replacing Stone Hill's native 0x00C2 package created a weird colored regular chest that gave a blue gem while the spring chest stayed inert. Appending the Peace Keepers T70/T71 pair displayed two Spring Chests but both stayed inert, including the shared-cluster flag4A-0x10 route. The current guarded candidate tests the same shared cluster with source-native +0x52 = 0xFF.
templates.note: Spring chest donor. Kept out of the normal Add Object list for beta because cross-level Spring Chest imports still misroute reward/effect behavior or crash in Stone Hill. Diagnostic candidate exports can still use this metadata.

templates.label: Key Chest
templates.dependencyRisk: Target-specific native runtime bundle. Artisans is verified for exactly one Key plus one Locked Chest; levels without a native 0x00AE chest still need their own handler, package, texture-allocation, and runtime-proof profile.
templates.testedResult: DuckStation verification passed in Artisans: the Key is golden, the Locked Chest uses the correct native texture, possession of the Key unlocks the chest, its six gem objects award +10 treasure once, and nearby level behavior remains normal.
templates.note: Artisans-only beta promotion of the runtime-proven V2 dependency bundle. Add Object exposes this as a Key + Key Chest pair; normal Create BIN supplies the native handler/model, five delayed reward markers, private texture rebases, persistence path, and checked WAD/EXE relocation. A second pair is intentionally blocked.

templates.label: Green Wizard
templates.dependencyRisk: Green Wizard is a full runtime bundle: actor/model animations, update handler, lightning actor, shared hurt/death paths, particles, textures, and per-instance properties/route data. The editor must use a target-level compatibility profile; copying only the source row or generic special data is unsafe.
templates.testedResult: The Toasty v11 standalone bundle passed runtime play. In native Wizard Peak, retired T10 v1 and v2 were visible, killable, and gem-paying but never attacked. The exact pod-matched T6-to-Elder-Wizard-T24 v3 route is runtime-proven: the user accepted visible lightning, the translated route, and one gem, while live RAM confirmed actor/model initialization, attack state, movement, death, and retirement.
templates.note: Replace-first Green Wizard template. In Wizard Peak, select Elder Wizard T24 for the runtime-proven native T6 in-place replacement; normal Create BIN and Create Swap Test compose this exact route. Retired T10 slots, all other targets, and true Add remain blocked. Other levels use only their explicitly profiled route.

templates.label: Green Wizard
templates.dependencyRisk: Blowhard already owns seven native actor 0x011B Wizard rows, but a replacement still needs a private rebased 0x40 properties block inside the real Moby-properties component, the target slot's pod/group, a translated one-point route, and pointer-fixup repair. Zero-looking collision-chain workspace is live runtime memory and is never allocation space.
templates.testedResult: Blowhard v2 passed DuckStation runtime play: repeated casts produced real lightning, two separate bolts damaged Spyro normally, the Wizard produced one death animation/sound and one gem, remained gone, and the surrounding area stayed normal.
templates.note: Hidden native Blowhard T0 donor for the Replace catalogue. Normal Create BIN and Create Swap Test both use the runtime-verified v2 recipe: grow the properties component by 0x40, shift pod/collision/fixup components byte-for-byte, preserve the destination pod/placement/yaw/reward, translate T0's route delta, and append the internal-pointer fixup. V1 is retired after its collision-memory alias caused repeat casts and death loops. The editor deliberately retains the dependency-aware existing-slot exporter boundary; it must not fall back to a generic source-record clone, and true Add remains unavailable.

templates.label: Green Wizard
templates.dependencyRisk: Magic Crafters already owns native actor 0x011B Wizard and actor 0x0026 lightning roots and handlers. The runtime-proven editor recipe is intentionally limited to T107 into T27: it installs a private 0x50-byte two-point properties block inside T27's unique 0x74-byte extent, preserves the trailing 0x24 bytes, and removes stale fixup 0xE9F8. A generic row clone or another destination remains unsafe without its own extent/fixup proof.
templates.testedResult: Magic Crafters v2 passed DuckStation runtime play. The real lightning strike hit Spyro while the Wizard's casting, attackability, death animation/sound, gem reward, retirement, and nearby behavior remained normal. Static guards freeze the unchanged scene components and the 0xBE-to-0xBD fixup repair.
templates.note: Hidden native Magic Crafters T107 donor for the verified T27 Replace path. The clean source row has state 0 even though the live cache reports state 1; staging retains clean state 0, source byte +0x4F value 0, +0x52 value 0x10, and the donor's raw renderer-distance byte 0x09. Normal Create BIN and Create Swap Test both compose the in-place v2 recipe. True Add, other donors, and other target slots remain unavailable until separately profiled.
